previous_disclosures.section: RISKS RELATED TO OUR OPERATING BUSINESSES
previous_disclosures.summary: The success of the core licensing business depends on licensees' ability to develop and deliver high-volume products with customer acceptance, over which Qualcomm has no control.

comparisons.peer_summary: Revenue from semi-custom SoC products depends on the success of customers' end products and the company's ability to secure design wins, with no control over customer marketing efforts, meaning actual revenue may not match expectations.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AMD disclose that their respective revenue streams depend heavily on the market success of products developed and sold by third parties (QCOM's licensees and AMD's semi-custom SoC customers), over which they have no control. QCOM explicitly states it has 'no control over the product development, sales efforts or pricing' of licensee products, mirroring AMD's disclosure that it has 'no control over the marketing efforts of these third parties' and that its revenue is 'directly related to sales of the third-party's products.'

sentences.text: Moreover, the success of our core licensing business depends in part on the ability of our licensees to continue to develop, introduce and deliver high-volume products that achieve and sustain customer acceptance.
We do not have control over the product development, sales efforts or pricing of products by our licensees, and our licensees might not be successful in these efforts.
Our revenue from our semi-custom SoC products is dependent upon our semi-custom SoC products being incorporated into customers' products and the success of those products.
Moreover, we have no control over the marketing efforts of these third parties, and we cannot make any assurances that sales of their products will be successful in current or future years.
Consequently, the semi-custom SoC product revenue expected by us may not be fully realized and our operating results may be adversely affected.

comparisons.peer_summary: Growth of the software business depends on customer acceptance of newer products and services.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and Broadcom highlight the risk that business success depends on 'customer acceptance' of products. QCOM's licensing revenue depends on licensees delivering 'high-volume products that achieve and sustain customer acceptance.' Similarly, Broadcom's software business growth depends on 'customer acceptance of our newer products and services.' While QCOM focuses on the downstream acceptance of licensee products and Broadcom on its own new software offerings, both identify customer acceptance as a critical, external dependency for revenue growth.

peer_results.rationale: Intel's candidates focus on competitive risks from new market entrants and the mechanics of electronic sales processes. These do not substantively address the specific dependency of revenue on third-party product development, customer acceptance of licensee/partner products, or lack of control over third-party marketing/sales, which are the core themes of QCOM's disclosure.

comparisons.peer_topic: System-Level Solution Development and Margin Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Development of system-level memory and storage products involves higher per-unit manufacturing costs, longer development cycles, and significant dependence on customer specifications and purchasing volumes, which may result in reduced profits if costs are not offset by higher prices.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and Micron disclose dependencies on third parties for product success, though the nature of the relationship differs. QCOM's revenue depends on licensees' ability to deliver high-volume products with customer acceptance, over which QCOM has no control. Micron discloses that its system-level solutions are dependent on 'customers choosing our products over those of our competitors and purchasing our products at sufficient volumes and prices,' noting that even if specifications are met, sales depend on customer selection. Both highlight that their financial outcomes are contingent on third-party decisions and market performance outside their direct control.

sentences.text: Moreover, the success of our core licensing business depends in part on the ability of our licensees to continue to develop, introduce and deliver high-volume products that achieve and sustain customer acceptance.
We do not have control over the product development, sales efforts or pricing of products by our licensees, and our licensees might not be successful in these efforts.

Even if our products meet customer specifications, our sales of system-level solutions are dependent upon our customers choosing our products over those of our competitors and purchasing our products at sufficient volumes and prices.

peer_results.rationale: NVIDIA's candidates focus on regulatory export control risks and third-party manufacturing supply chain dependencies. These are distinct from QCOM's disclosure regarding commercial dependency on licensee product success and customer acceptance, with no overlap in the specific business driver or risk mechanism described.
